Business name: Willow Tea Room
Selected business type: Tea Shop
Business description / notes: Figures are monthly and in USD. The Tuesday late sitting, 6 PM until 10 PM, took USD 1,650; wages assigned to that sitting came to USD 2,750. There were 5 people on duty. Friday evenings had 5 on duty and took USD 6,800 for the month.
Owner's reply to the rota manager: You have my go-ahead for a trial on Tuesday evenings from 6 PM to 10 PM. Take 1 person off that sitting's roster and see how it goes.
The remainder of the weekly rota is to stay exactly as it is; do not move or cut staff on other shifts.

leaks.title: Tuesday late sitting labor cost exceeds revenue with same staffing as higher-revenue Friday
evidence: Tuesday late sitting (6 PM–10 PM) generated USD 1,650 in revenue and incurred USD 2,750 in wages with 5 staff on duty.
Friday evenings generated USD 6,800 in revenue with the same staffing level of 5 people on duty.
Owner authorized a trial removing 1 person from the Tuesday evening roster while keeping the rest of the weekly rota unchanged.
leaks.interpretation: The Tuesday late sitting operates with a significant revenue-to-wage gap (USD 1,650 revenue vs USD 2,750 wages) while using identical staffing to Friday evenings, which generate over four times the revenue. The owner has explicitly approved a controlled test reducing Tuesday staffing by one person, indicating recognition of potential overstaffing for that shift.

insufficient_evidence.reason: No evidence provided on ingredient waste rates, targets, or costs to assess whether waste is a profit leak.
No evidence provided on delivery orders, platform fees, packaging costs, or food costs to evaluate delivery profitability.
Total monthly operating costs and rent amounts are not provided, preventing assessment of whether fixed costs are excessive relative to revenue.
No ingredient cost data or benchmarks provided to determine if ingredient purchasing is inefficient.
Staffing levels and revenue for days/shifts other than Tuesday late sitting and Friday evenings are not provided, so labor efficiency elsewhere cannot be evaluated.
